instructions: Pull the stems off the 4 guajillo and 3 ancho chiles. Tear them open and shake out the seeds.

Heat a large dry skillet over medium. Lay in the chiles and toast them for 2 to 3 minutes, turning them often, until they smell toasty and soften a little. Watch them closely. Burnt chiles make the sauce bitter.
Cut three quarters of the onion into large chunks and peel the 2 garlic cloves. Put the chiles, onion chunks and garlic in a saucepan and pour in enough water to cover them.
Bring the saucepan to a simmer over medium high and simmer for 10 minutes, pushing the chiles under now and then, until they're soft and floppy.

Meanwhile, cut the 2 lb chuck roast into 2 inch cubes and pat them dry. Season them with 1 tsp of the salt and the 1/2 tsp pepper, then toss them with the 1 1/2 tbsp flour until every side has a light coat.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a Dutch oven over medium high. Add half the beef in a single layer with room between the pieces. Leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is deep brown and lets go of the pan, then turn the cubes and brown the other sides, about 5 minutes. Move them to a plate. Stand back a little. It spatters.
Add the last 1 tbsp oil to the pot and brown the second batch of beef the same way. Move it to the plate with the first batch.

Lift the chiles, onion and garlic into a blender with a slotted spoon. Add 1 cup of the soaking water, the 1 3/4 cups broth, the 1 1/2 tsp cumin, the 1 1/2 tsp coriander, the 1 tsp oregano and the remaining 1/2 tsp salt. Hold the lid down with a folded towel and blend for about 1 minute, until the sauce is completely smooth.

Pour off all but a thin film of fat from the Dutch oven. Pour in the sauce and scrape up the browned bits on the bottom with a wooden spoon. Put the beef and any juices from the plate back in and tuck in the 2 bay leaves.

Bring it to a gentle bubble, cover the pot and turn the heat to low. Simmer for 2 hours, stirring every half hour so nothing sticks to the bottom. It's ready when a cube of beef falls apart when you press it with a fork.
Meanwhile, finely dice the last quarter of the onion. Chop a large handful of the cilantro, thinly slice 4 of the radishes and cut the lime into wedges.
Take out the bay leaves and spoon off any oil sitting on the top. Taste the sauce. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt or a squeeze of the lime.
Warm each tortilla in a dry skillet over medium for about 30 seconds, flip it and warm the other side for 30 seconds. Stack them in a clean towel as you go.
Serve with the warm tortillas, with the diced onion, cilantro, radishes and lime wedges on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions brown cubed chuck, make a smooth red sauce from dried chiles and simmer the beef in it for about 2 hours until it falls apart. So Much Food toasts guajillo, ancho and a little chile de arbol, simmers them with onion and garlic, blends them with cumin, coriander, oregano and broth, and browns the beef in a light coat of flour so the sauce thickens as it cooks. A Family Feast soaks the chiles in hot stock and adds molasses and red wine vinegar, and Zestful Kitchen fries tomato paste with the aromatics and finishes with lime and cilantro. This one follows So Much Food at two thirds of its amounts and leaves out the chile de arbol so the pot stays mild.
